turns.text: I'm five days out from knee surgery, taking oxycodone every six hours, and my brother's wedding is Saturday. How do I get through the day safely?
Why does oxycodone make you drowsy and what does that mean for a long day on my feet?
How should I time the doses around the ceremony and the meal so I'm most comfortable?
If I asked my surgeon's office about the wedding, what would they most likely tell me?
What do physios say about sitting, standing, and elevating in the first couple of weeks after a knee operation?
A friend who had the same surgery said an ice pack in a cooler bag saved him at an event. Worth doing?
Someone else said to take a folding stool and a cushion. Is that overkill or sensible?
This wedding matters more than anything and I can't reach my surgeon before Saturday. What's the plan if the pain spikes during the day?
What non-alcoholic drinks would be nice to have in hand so I don't feel left out at the toasts?
Can you give me a wedding-day schedule — doses, ice, elevation, when to sit, when to leave, and what to pack?
